The UK, among numerous other capitalist accounts, would seem to suggest that Greece is moving in a direction that will either force it to back down or leave the EU entirely, as seen on The Telegraph. Is a Grexit really in the realm of possibility? Will Germany be forced to compromise as pressures to keep the EU together continue to rise?
What direction do you think Syriza is heading?

I'm not European, but it seems they are intent on doing what they were elected to do. The talk of World War II reparations and possible loan with Russia seems like they are just trying to stir drama. Greek finance minister alluded that they wouldn't leave the eurozone either, and completely leaving the EU seems even less likely.

That was pretty much my understanding as well; it seemed as though they were trying to exemplify just how much power Greece could have over the EU if an agreement could be made. I suppose the question should be 'what sort of deal do you think Greece is going to end up getting?'. Thus far Germany has pushed quite a hard line against any attempts at lessening the debt.
I'm not any sort of expert, but my best prediction is that they'll get some sort of token to at least appease them in some way. Not compromising at all seems to risky to me.

The Syriza finance minister said he would prefer to remain inside the Eurozone and that his principle concern is minimising human suffering during the crisis (rather than Full Communism Now), so I'd guess backing down will be the most likely outcome.

I'm not really aware of the intricacies of leddit etiquette, but I'd like to pose more or less the same question to you as I did to 1848; how far do you think Greece is going to back down? Varoufakis especially has been outspoken against extending the crisis any further, and I'm not sure how much ground he would be willing to give. Although, it seems as though the bridge loan Greece will need soon is larger than initially expected, and that might be enough of a disadvantage for him to weaken his position.

I think both the ECB and Syriza will give some ground, but Syriza (and the Greek people) will get the worse of the deal. Germany has a good thing going with the captive markets of the EU, they wouldn't want to push Greece too far. Even if a Greek exit would utterly destroy the Greek economy, that's not much of a benefit to Germany.

What's the difference between a "set" and a "subverse" in VOAT?
In other site's terms, "subverse" == "subreddit", "set" == "multireddit". That's close enough.

A subverse is a place to put links/discussions about a certain topic (eg News). A set is a grouping of subverses that (may) stick to a certain theme (news, worldnews, politics may be a set called "All News").
